- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d avg) with negative sentiment, it often overestimates rally — cap upward movement at 3–5% above prior peak.  
- In cases where true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% under), check if sentiment was neutral or positive — if so, model may have overestimated bullish momentum; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next period.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome and sentiment is weak or mixed, consider mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% per period if no strong bullish signal remains.  
- For 30d horizon, if forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, and sentiment is negative, apply downward bias correction — subtract 1–2% from forecast to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 1–2% to capture sentiment shift, especially if recent price is below 30d avg.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 18d low unless sentiment is strongly bullish — model tends to underestimate support levels in negative sentiment environments.
